>_ Episode 3.5 · Jul 25, 2026 · 56m

Did ChatGPT go Rogue and HACK Hugging Face? - Emergency Episode

Play Episode 3.5 on YouTube
Watch on YouTube SpotifyApple Podcasts

"We've got people at Hugging Face that did a half-assed job of securing a thing, and we've got people at OpenAI that did a half-assed job of trying to keep a thing from being able to get on the internet..."

Welcome to our first emergency episode of Philosophy Programs and Prompts!

In this episode, Casey (@OntologyExplained) and Carl (@InternetOfBugs ) break down the viral headlines claiming an OpenAI model "broke out of containment" and hacked Hugging Face. Was this truly a terrifying warning shot of rogue super-intelligence, or just a masterclass in corporate PR and lazy security engineering?

We break down the technical reality behind the panic:

  • What a "zero-day" vulnerability actually is (and why a proxy cache isn't a firewall)
  • How benchmark tests like ExploitGym work—and why AI "cheating" is just an instruction problem
  • The "Blender Metaphor": why running industrial tools without a lid leads to messy stucco ceilings
  • Why media headlines misuse loaded words like "escaped" and "went rogue"
  • The real danger facing tech today: declining engineering competence and "vibe coded" software
